messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: service=redwood-inference-prod-auth, escalation_policy=contractors-night, urgency=high — <https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-89123|PD-89123>
Irene Chen: wait, the service is prod-auth? we shouldn't be routing to contractors for prod.
Sam K: confirmed — PD link shows 'contractors-night' as the escalation. I just changed a schedule earlier today but I targeted staging rotas only.
Mica Patel: who got paged? contractor-ops?
ops-bot: Notifying @contractor-ops (primary). Pager history: auto-escalation -> acknowledged by contractor-ops at 1759000102.
contractor-ops: acked, but we're not set up for prod-level runbook. forwarding to ops-sre. pinging oncall.
Irene Chen: @Sam K can you check the schedule change? this looks like a schedule binding got applied to the wrong PD service.
Sam K: looking now — the script I ran replaced schedule id "sched-2024-night" globally due to a bad grep; I thought it was limited to /staging/ but the service filter was empty. my bad.
Mica Patel: okay immediate mitigation: can we remove contractors-night from prod-auth escalation and rebind to ops-sre?
Sam K: doing a manual override now.
ops-bot: Command run: ```pd service update redwood-inference-prod-auth --escalation-policy ops-sre-primary``` -> success at 1759000258
incident-bot: PD update received, escalation policy set to ops-sre-primary. auto-notifications suppressed for contractors-night.
contractor-ops: thanks — we stood down and unacked, confirmed no further alerts from that service.
Irene Chen: customer impact? any live user-facing errors reported?
Mica Patel: Cloud metrics show an auth latency spike 1759000000–1759000300, error rate up ~4% (mainly 401s) — likely a brief token validation cache miss from the deploy at 1758999980. partially mitigated when ops team rolled credentials refresh.
Sam K: short narrative: bad schedule change + deploy overlap caused wrong escalation and some auth failures. no widespread data loss. some customers on EU region reported degraded auth.
Irene Chen: thanks. immediate action items: 1) revert my global schedule-edit script change (Sam) 2) add a safety filter when updating schedules (Sam) 3) run PD audit to find other services bound to contractors-night (Mica) 4) notify contracts and ops leadership (Irene).
Sam K: will open PR to add `--env` require flag and a dry-run validation. PR link: <https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge_requests/482>
Mica Patel: running PD audit now: ```pd service list --query "escalation_policy:contractors-night"``` -> returns 1 hit (redwood-inference-prod-auth).
ops-bot: Incident notes appended to PD: PD-89123 — wrong escalation policy applied by infra script; mitigation performed; followup assigned.
contractor-ops: no further action needed from contractors. please cc us on postmortem for lessons learned.
Irene Chen: assigning follow-up: owner=Mica Patel, due=1759080000, scope=postmortem+automation fixes.
Mica Patel: ack. I'll include timeline, root cause (missing service filter), and checklist for schedule changes.
Sam K: sorry everyone — will patch and run broader audit tonight.
Irene Chen: can we also add an automated guard in the deploy script to check for accidental global matches? something like: ```if [[ -z "$ENV_FILTER" ]]; then exit 1; fi```
Sam K: yes adding that to preflight.
Mica Patel: tagging oncall + support to reach out to EU customers affected. support thread: <https://support.internal/ticket/INC-4567>
incident-bot: Incident closed in PagerDuty (PD-89123) at 1759000745 — status: resolved, resolved_by=ops-sre-primary.
Irene Chen: short-term postmortem planned. thanks for quick responses. :thumbsup:
